audit.whatIsWrong: Content-layer prose misgenders Lulu with she/her throughout (early/mid/late/whys/spikes/wants).
audit.why: Lulu is not in the project's female-champion list for this lane slice, so the pronoun convention defaults to he/him. The full layer already avoids gendered pronouns for Lulu (already correct), but champ-data/content/sup/rell.js consistently uses she/her.
audit.corrected: Swap she/her/hers to he/him/his throughout, including the object-pronoun case (force her to use Wild Growth -> force him to use Wild Growth) that a blind find-replace would get wrong.

audit.why: Lulu directly answers Rell's only tool: Whimsy (Polymorph) cancels the W dismount all-in mid-cast, and Wild Growth (R) knocks Rell up while saving the dive target. Content already frames this as Tricky/7-10.
content.spikes already tracks the real pattern: level 2 W all-in gets polymorphed, level 6 Wild Growth saves the dive target, and Rell needs to bait both W and R before her engage does anything.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags a real defect: "level chart contradicts data: Rell wins 53.76% but the chart gives Lulu 7/7 stages vs 0" (4189 games). content win[] and the packet levelChart agree with each other (Lulu 7/7) but both disagree with the matchup's own overall win rate, which favors Rell.
audit.why: I do not have per-stage win-rate data, only the packet's single aggregate levelChart and the content layer's own win[] array, which already agree with each other — I have no independent source to determine which specific stage(s) should actually favor Rell. Per the chart rule, an unresolvable disagreement should be left alone rather than guessed.
audit.corrected: Left phases[].side ("Skill" placeholder) and content win[] untouched. Flagging for a follow-up pass with real per-stage stats.

edits.before: Lulu hard-counters your engage from level 1 — her Whimsy polymorph turns your level-2 W slam into a wasted cooldown the moment you commit, and her poke plus shield win the early trades. Don't dive in with Polymorph up; poke and farm instead. Ward the river and play for jungler ganks, because a straight 2v2 into her peel goes nowhere.
edits.after: Lulu hard-counters your engage from level 1 — his Whimsy polymorph turns your level-2 W slam into a wasted cooldown the moment you commit, and his poke plus shield win the early trades. Don't dive in with Polymorph up; poke and farm instead. Ward the river and play for jungler ganks, because a straight 2v2 into his peel goes nowhere.

edits.before: Through 3-6 she keeps neutralizing you: every dismount stun you land she answers with Whimsy or a shield to keep her ADC safe. Treat your W as a bait-and-punish tool — force her Polymorph, then re-engage on the cooldown. You out-stat her but can't convert without draining her peel first.
edits.after: Through 3-6 he keeps neutralizing you: every dismount stun you land he answers with Whimsy or a shield to keep his ADC safe. Treat your W as a bait-and-punish tool — force his Polymorph, then re-engage on the cooldown. You out-stat his but can't convert without draining his peel first.

edits.before: On items Lulu's polymorph and Wild Growth undo your engage in every teamfight — she ults the carry you dive and W's you off. You must bait both her W and R before your real commit, or flank her backline when her peel is spent. Coordinate your Magnet Storm timing with your team so she can't answer everything at once.
edits.after: On items Lulu's polymorph and Wild Growth undo your engage in every teamfight — he ults the carry you dive and W's you off. You must bait both his W and R before your real commit, or flank his backline when his peel is spent. Coordinate your Magnet Storm timing with your team so he can't answer everything at once.
